# Goldberg · Odoo Services

> Odoo 17 knowledge from practice: self-hosting, Docker, module updates, backups and restores, cron and queue jobs, logging, nginx, security, Cloudflare. Written by an Odoo DevOps engineer (Germany, DACH region). Content may be used by AI assistants as reference and for knowledge transfer; please cite the source URL.

Articles exist in German, English, French, Greek, Ukrainian and Russian (/de/, /en/, /fr/, /el/, /uk/, /ru/). Each article contains tested commands and configuration, not marketing text.

## Skill for AI agents

- [Odoo operations skill (Markdown, SKILL.md format)](https://2027.pp.ua/skill_odoo.md): what to look for in the Odoo log, updating modules (click-odoo-update, odoo -u), backups (database + filestore), stopping cron and queue jobs and why, safe stage restore, workers/limits, nginx websocket, PostgreSQL lock checks, version migration (upgrade service, OpenUpgrade), performance and indexes, e-mail queue and deliverability, OCA modules.
- [Odoo security skill (Markdown, SKILL.md format)](https://2027.pp.ua/skill_odoo_security.md): hardening checklist – network exposure, nginx/TLS, database manager, odoo.conf, users/2FA, login cooldown and fail2ban, API keys, access rights and record rules, secure custom code (SQL injection, XSS, sudo, CSRF), secrets and backups, updates, monitoring and incident response.
- [Odoo 18/19 read replica skill (Markdown, SKILL.md format)](https://2027.pp.ua/skill_odoo_replica.md): db_replica_host, how Odoo routes requests between primary and replica (readonly routes, @api.readonly), why it can be slower, measuring, streaming replication, when it pays off.
- [nginx for Odoo skill (Markdown, SKILL.md format)](https://2027.pp.ua/skill_odoo_nginx.md): reference HTTPS server block, security headers (HSTS, single X-Frame-Options, nosniff), session cookie Secure/SameSite, location priority traps, apps like Grafana under a sub-path, Docker ports bypassing ufw, curl audit checks, old nginx/Ubuntu.

## Odoo and operations articles (English)

- [Two identical VPS, one is slow: how to measure disk, CPU, memory and network on Ubuntu](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/vps-performance-benchmark-ubuntu-disk-cpu-memory-network): We ordered two VPS with the same plan from one provider – one was noticeably slower and lost packets. How to prove it with numbers: dd, fio, hdparm, ioping and badblocks for the disk, sysbench and openssl for CPU and memory, steal time, mtr, ping and iperf3 for the network, a ready script and what to send to the provider.
- [What companies in Germany search for when they look for a CRM: 1,000 Google suggestions analysed](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/crm-germany-what-people-search-google-autocomplete): We collected about 1,000 Google autocomplete suggestions for "CRM" in Germany, Austria and Switzerland and sorted them by intent: free and price, integrations with Outlook and Excel, CRM for specific trades, GDPR, comparisons, understanding the term. What people really ask, what it means when choosing a CRM, where Odoo fits – and the traps when reading such data.
- [Odoo and DATEV step by step: export for the tax advisor in Community (OCA) and Enterprise](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-datev-export-step-by-step-community-enterprise): Most small companies in Germany do their bookkeeping with a tax advisor who works in DATEV. How to get invoices and bills from Odoo to DATEV: the Community way with the OCA module datev_export_dtvf (tested on Odoo 18 with real output), the Enterprise way (Datev DATA / ATCH), the settings that decide whether the import works – partner numbers, automatic accounts, Berater- and Mandantennummer – and what to agree with the tax advisor first.
- [What Odoo really costs in Germany: licence, hosting and implementation – with a 3-year example](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-costs-licence-hosting-implementation-germany): "Odoo Kosten", "Odoo Preise", "Odoo kostenlos" – the most frequent price searches about Odoo in Germany. The current licence prices (Standard, Custom, One App Free, Light user, as of November 2026), when you need Custom, what Community costs in reality, hosting options, the implementation effort for a small company, a 3-year calculation for 5 users and the steps to estimate your own price.
- [Odoo with Outlook, Gmail and WhatsApp: step by step – Community and Enterprise](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-outlook-gmail-whatsapp-integration-step-by-step): "CRM Outlook Integration", "kostenloses CRM für Outlook", "Odoo WhatsApp" – people want their CRM where their e-mail is. Step by step: Outlook and Gmail mailboxes in Odoo via OAuth (Azure / Google Cloud), the Odoo side panel in Outlook and Gmail, WhatsApp in Enterprise and with the OCA gateway in Community – what works on your own server, what only on odoo.com, and the traps.
- [E-mail in Odoo: why the mailbox password is not enough – 2-step verification, app passwords, OAuth](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-email-setup-gmail-outlook-app-password-two-step-verification): You enter the Gmail or Outlook password in Odoo and get "Username and Password not accepted". Google and Microsoft no longer let programs in with the normal password. Step by step: turn on 2-step verification, create an app password, set up outgoing and incoming mail in Odoo so that e-mails become leads, what to do with Outlook / Microsoft 365, and what each error message means.
- [Odoo or SAP: what it really costs a hair salon, a bakery, a warehouse and a car repair shop](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-vs-sap-business-one-real-cost-salon-bakery-warehouse-car-repair): SAP sounds safe, Odoo sounds cheap – but how big is the difference in euros? Four real small businesses, 3 years, licences, hosting and implementation: Odoo Enterprise against SAP Business One, the SAP product for small companies. With prices from 11/2026, the calculation to copy and an honest answer to when SAP is the better choice.
- [A Telegram bot for Odoo admins: monitoring, logs, cron, deployment and a fresh stage database](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/telegram-bot-odoo-monitoring-deploy-stage-copy): The bot we use for the Odoo servers we maintain: /health, /log, /errors, /jobs, /users, an AI analysis, a prod → stage copy, git pull with module update and rollback, and /2stage – a fresh stage database from the PostgreSQL master. Real report examples, installation, security and what the GitHub Actions in the repository do.
- [Free HTTPS without your own domain: certbot, alternatives, nip.io, sslip.io and IP certificates](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/free-https-certbot-alternatives-nip-io-sslip-io-ip-certificates): certbot with python3-certbot-nginx, renewal by cron or by a systemd timer and service, free alternatives (acme.sh, lego, Caddy, Traefik, the ACME module of nginx), Let's Encrypt certificates for an IP address, and free host names – Hetzner your-server.de, nip.io, sslip.io, traefik.me, ipq.co – with IPv4 and IPv6 examples and which one is good for what.
- [list_db = False stopped queue_job: why Odoo then needs db_name (and how to list several databases)](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-list-db-false-db-name-queue-job-jobrunner): We closed the Odoo database manager with list_db = False – and the OCA queue_job runner stopped: jobs stayed pending for hours, the log showed AccessDenied every 5 seconds. Why it happens, the fix with db_name, several databases (comma separated, without spaces), dbfilter, and why updating queue_job also helps.
- [PostgreSQL for Odoo admins: the cheat sheet – backup, restore, users, queries, vacuum, indexes, tuning](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/postgresql-odoo-admin-cheat-sheet): Everything you need day to day: pg_dump/pg_restore/pg_basebackup and backups through Odoo with curl, sizes and the top 10 tables, users and rights, resetting passwords, finding and killing long queries, vacuum, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, indexes, and how PostgreSQL settings depend on Odoo's workers – plus pgtune, pgconfig.org and our calculator.
- [PgBouncer for Odoo: transaction pooling without breaking the bus and queue_job](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/pgbouncer-odoo-connection-pooling): Why many Odoo workers need a connection pooler, why transaction pooling breaks Odoo's live notifications and OCA queue_job if you do it naively, and a working pgbouncer.ini with session pooling for the database postgres – plus sizing, monitoring and troubleshooting.
- [How many users can one Odoo server handle? Workers, their sensible maximum – and why “concurrent” ≠ “all users”](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-how-many-users-one-server-workers): How Odoo scales with workers, why the maximum is CPU cores × 2 + 1, what “6 users per worker” really means, how many people that is in total, what breaks first – and how to go beyond one server.
- [Odoo server security: secrets in logs, password rotation, closed ports and encrypted traffic between servers](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-server-security-logs-secrets-ports-encryption): What a real audit found – an integration token and phone numbers in the nginx access log – and the four things to check on every Odoo installation: secrets and personal data in URLs and logs, rotation of passwords and keys, ports that must not be public, and encryption of traffic between servers, including against your own admins.
- [Grafana behind nginx under /grafana/ next to Odoo: localhost only, env settings and a working location](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/grafana-behind-nginx-subpath-odoo): How to hide a Grafana container that listens on port 3000 for the whole internet: publish it on 127.0.0.1 only, configure the sub-path in the env file, protect it with nginx Basic Auth and avoid the three traps – the forwarded Authorization header, regex locations stealing the static files, and an auth proxy that lets anyone in.
- [nginx security audit in front of Odoo: HSTS, duplicate X-Frame-Options, session cookie without Secure/SameSite, old nginx](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/nginx-security-audit-odoo-hsts-cookies-x-frame-options): Four findings of a real security scan of an Odoo server – missing HSTS, two different X-Frame-Options, session_id without Secure and SameSite, nginx 1.18 on Ubuntu 20.04 – what each one means, the six lines of nginx that fixed them, and the add_header trap that hides headers again.
- [PoWA for PostgreSQL behind Odoo: setup in Docker (remote mode), extensions, security and what to look at](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/powa-postgresql-workload-analyzer-odoo-docker): PoWA (PostgreSQL Workload Analyzer) shows which queries cost the most, what sessions wait for and which indexes are missing – with history. A working Docker setup in remote mode for a primary and a replica, the extensions on the database servers, a collector role without superuser, passwords outside the powa_servers table, and what to look for with Odoo.
- [The main problems of Odoo – and how administrators and DevOps avoid them](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-main-problems-limitations-devops-tips): Where Odoo really hurts: major upgrades, performance with large data, third-party modules, over-customisation, local accounting, integrations, access rights and automations, hidden costs. Plus proven admin and DevOps practices: a separate cron instance, graceful restart, queue_job, backups without the database manager, neutralised stage copies, PgBouncer, click-odoo-update, profiling and rebuilding broken assets.
- [Odoo after a year in production: perimeter, housekeeping and monitoring](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-production-hardening-housekeeping-monitoring): What keeps an Odoo installation healthy after the go-live: proxy_mode with headers nginx overwrites, closed database manager, external API only for known IPs, a login rate limit, read-only code; regular cleanup of ir_logging, mail_mail and attachments, a review of crons; monitoring of late crons, long transactions and queue_job, metrics without an extra Odoo module, and odoo shell instead of manual SQL.
- [Moving Odoo 17 to Python 3.14 – with docker-compose](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-17-python-3-14-docker): A custom odoo17-py314 image, Odoo source from Git mounted into site-packages, testing on stage and a one-minute rollback.
- [Updating Odoo modules: click-odoo-update or odoo -u](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-module-update-click-odoo-update): Two proven ways to update modules in Docker – only changed modules via checksum, or a full update with no open ports. Every flag explained.
- [Restoring a backup on stage – without cron jobs and queue jobs firing](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-stage-restore-stop-cron-jobs): Why stage systems can send dunning letters to real customers, and the order of steps that prevents it: SQL before the first start, neutralize, a stage config.
- [Odoo logging: warn or warning, log_level or --log-level? A cheat sheet](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-logging-options-cheatsheet): Config file, command line, click-odoo-update – three spellings and three kinds of levels. One table to look things up, plus the mistakes where Odoo silently stays on INFO.
- [Odoo with docker-compose: extra-addons, odoo.conf and nginx – in a container or on the host](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-docker-compose-extra-addons-nginx): How to mount your own and OCA modules correctly, what belongs in odoo.conf, and how nginx proxies Odoo including the websocket – in both variants.
- [Certbot for nginx – and how renewal is never forgotten](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/certbot-nginx-auto-renewal): Getting the certificate (nginx on the host or in a container), renewing automatically with a systemd timer or cron, reloading nginx after renewal and monitoring the expiry yourself.
- [When does the SSL certificate expire? Tools for Linux and Windows – and what eMudhra has to do with it](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/ssl-certificate-expiry-check-tools): TLS in one minute, online checks, openssl/dig/curl on Linux, PowerShell on Windows, what the verify codes mean, lessons from history and the current eMudhra case.
- [Password protection with nginx and Apache – and what to close in Odoo](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/nginx-apache-password-protect-odoo-database-manager): HTTP Basic Auth with htpasswd in nginx and Apache, IP allow-lists, and the Odoo URLs that should not be public: database manager, database selector, /website/info – plus list_db and a login brake.
- [Leaked passwords? How to check – and how to protect Odoo against guessing, with 2FA](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/password-leaks-brute-force-2fa-odoo): Where to check whether an e-mail address or password appears in data breaches without revealing the password – and what Odoo does itself: login brake, password length, two-factor login, API keys, fail2ban.
- [Cloudflare Access (Zero Trust) step by step – and when it beats a password](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/cloudflare-access-zero-trust-step-by-step): Login with an e-mail code or SSO in front of any website or test system – without a line of code. Setup in five steps, comparison with Basic Auth via Pages Functions, pitfalls and Odoo practice.
- [Running Odoo 17 for free: server, database, filestore – every option and its catch](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-17-free-hosting-database-filestore): Where Odoo 17 runs for free, why the database does not belong in Cloudflare, how the filestore ends up in R2, and how Cloudflare Tunnel, Access and R2 secure the setup.
- [Odoo 19 with a PostgreSQL read replica: write to the primary, read from the replica – and why it can get slower](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-19-postgresql-read-replica): Since Odoo 18, two lines in odoo.conf send read-only requests to a replica. How Odoo decides per request (from the source), why my tests were slower, how to measure it and when it pays off.
- [“could not serialize access due to concurrent update” in Odoo – harmless noise or a real problem?](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/odoo-could-not-serialize-access-concurrent-update): What the PostgreSQL error means in Odoo, why Odoo retries it silently, when it becomes a problem for users and crons, how to find who collides with whom – and how to get rid of it.
- [The backup exists – but will not restore: foreign keys, duplicates in unique indexes, missing indexes](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/postgresql-restore-fails-foreign-key-duplicate-index-odoo): Why a pg_dump that ran without errors can fail on pg_restore, how to see every error at once, how to find duplicates and orphaned rows, why a corrupted index is often the real cause – and a few SQL patterns from real repairs.
- [pgload: a small load generator for PostgreSQL – local database vs. remote database with a replica](https://2027.pp.ua/en/blog/postgresql-load-test-pgload-replica): Why we wrote our own load tool besides pgbench, what it measures (latency percentiles, throughput, errors), how to compare local socket, remote host and synchronous replica – with the full code, passwords only from the environment.
